_meta.law: source of truth for collections. a collection holds pages of one section (section field - pages live under pages/<section>/collections/). a multi-collection holds collections. engine: tools/build.py.

collections.title: The Complete Hitman
collections.caption: the four classic hits, 2002 to 2012, plus the console remasters that complete the line.
about: Every Hitman entry the catalogue carries, in one place: Silent Assassin (2002), Contracts (2004), Blood Money (2006) and Absolution (2012) - the four windows builds this archive digs - plus the two console remaster lines that sit above them. The 2013 Hitman HD Trilogy rebuilt Silent Assassin, Contracts and Blood Money for ps3 and xbox 360; the 2019 Hitman HD Enhanced Collection rebuilt Blood Money and Absolution at 4k/60 for ps4 and xbox one. Neither remaster ever shipped a windows build, so on pc the four originals remain the real thing - both remaster pages document their lines honestly from the console side.

Codename 47, the World of Assassination trilogy and the spin-offs (GO, Sniper, Sniper Challenge) sit outside the current catalogue; they appear in the series strips as reference only. Six pages, one contract.
notes: Codename 47, the World of Assassination trilogy and the spin-offs (GO, Sniper, Sniper Challenge) sit outside the current catalogue; they appear in the series strips as reference only.

collections.title: The Complete Chicken Invaders
collections.caption: the complete line: five wars, their remasters written one by one, and the universe - 1999 to today.
about: The full Chicken Invaders line from InterAction studios: the five classic wars with every holiday release living as a version under its episode's page (four Christmas editions, two Easter editions, one Halloween, one Thanksgiving - switched from the dropdown, not scattered as standalone entries), plus the three things that complete the family: the per-episode remasters, the episodic rework, and Universe.

One production quirk stays on record: the third war's Christmas Edition (November 2006) shipped three months before the standard game (January 2007), making it the only edition in the series that predates its own episode.

InterAction studios is alive and every entry remains officially obtainable: the studio's download hub carries the classic line, Steam sells the mainline episodes and five of the eight holiday editions as DLC (the second and third wars' Christmas editions, the fourth war's Thanksgiving, and both fifth-war editions - the rest live on the studio's own store), and Universe is free to play. These pages are ownership stories, not rescues - the archive links ride along for preservation.

A sequel is never an upgrade, and the pages keep that law one war at a time: the first war's rebuild is Chicken Invaders Remastered (2023), the second war's is The Next Wave Remastered (2012), and the later wars ride the Episodes rework (2025) instead - no classic-engine remaster was ever made for wars three to five. Every classic page names its own rebuild, and every rebuild has its own page.
notes: The two remaster entries cover only their own war: Remastered (2023) is the first war's rebuild, The Next Wave Remastered (2012) is the second's. Episode 1: The Saga Begins is the new-engine remake of the first war, and the Episodes page carries the free rework line for wars two to five, version by version.

collections.title: The Dash Universe
collections.caption: PlayFirst's DinerTown empire: every Dash game of the pc era, one universe.
about: Diner Dash (2003) by gameLab and PlayFirst turned restaurant time-management into a franchise and its waitress Flo into a casual-gaming icon. The pc line it built runs a full decade: Restaurant Rescue (2006), Flo on the Go (2006), Hometown Hero (2007) - with the Once Upon a Diner story expansion and the standalone Seasonal Snack Pack riding beside it - Flo Through Time (2008) and Boom! (2010) carry the numbered story, and the formula spun off into whole sub-lines - Wedding Dash ran 2007-2010 across four games, Cooking Dash 2008-2010 across three (its Thrills & Spills entry shipped a collector's edition with an exclusive Klondike Gold Rush stage), Hotel Dash 2009-2011 across two, and Avenue Flo (2009-2010) turned the waitress into a point-and-click adventurer. The collector's-edition line matters here: Boom!'s 2012 collector's edition added five exclusive advanced levels and a strategy guide, and it has its own page through the Boom! entry.

The DinerTown side line filled out the town itself: Doggie, Dairy, Fashion, Parking, Fitness, Diaper and Garden Dash (2008-2011) moved the chained-service engine to spas, farms, studios, lots, gyms, daycares and gardens, DinerTown Tycoon (2009) stretched it into a business sim, DinerTown Detective Agency (2009) went hidden-object, Soap Opera Dash (2008) ran the loop on a tv studio set, and two licensed SpongeBob SquarePants crossovers (2006-2007) carried it onto Nickelodeon's turf. Thirty-one titles, one universe, all of it the pc era.

The shelf's state is mixed and honest about it: seven of the thirty-one still sell on Steam (Hometown Hero, Cooking Dash, Wedding Dash 2, Hotel Dash: Suite Success, Fitness Dash, Diaper Dash and DinerTown Tycoon), while the rest died with their channels - PlayFirst folded into Glu Mobile in 2014, playfirst.com is gone, and the download portals closed with it. The un-buyable cases are the archive's rescue lane: no store, no key server, preserved anyway.

Scope law for this collection: windows builds only. The mobile free-to-play era that followed the classic line is outside this collection - the Deluxe re-releases (Diner Dash Deluxe, SpongeBob Diner Dash Deluxe) and Diner Dash Rush, Diner Dash (2014) and Diner Dash Adventures all belong to phones, and phones are out of scope for this archive. Each entry below is its own dug page with its own sources, sizes and archive routes.

collections.title: Grand Theft Auto
collections.caption: the 3d-era pair and the modern giants - three pages carrying the whole pc line this archive digs.
about: The grand theft auto row this catalogue carries runs three pages: the classic san andreas & vice city pairing, gta iv and gta v. The direct line reads in order - vice city (2002), san andreas (2004) as the 3d-era peaks bundled together here, then gta iv (2008) rebooting the tone in liberty city, then gta v (2013/2015) splitting the lead three ways in los santos.

Each step is a sequel, not an upgrade: none of these replaces another, and the classics stay the only versions of themselves since rockstar delisted them. The bundle page documents both classic builds; the remaster-era definitive editions live outside this catalogue and are named where relevant.
notes: the classic builds are delisted - their archive routes live on the bundle page.

collections.title: PopCap Classics
collections.caption: the pre-merger and ea-era popcap shelf - every deluxe build the catalogue carries, still smiling.
about: PopCap's deluxe era is the spine of the casual shelf: zuma, peggle, bejeweled 3, chuzzle, dynomite, insaniquarium, heavy weapon, plants vs. zombies, plus the post-merger doors for astropop, big money and talismania, and the archive-only stock the current stores never carried - bookworm adventures, atomica, pixelus, qbeez whirled, seven seas, tiptop, venice and rocket mania.

Every row keeps its own page; a handful also sit in the marble poppers collection because the mechanics put them there. The collection view is exactly that - one shelf, sorted by nothing but belonging.

collections.title: Marble Poppers
collections.caption: the chain-shooter line - zuma's law, luxor's temples and every track that rolls.
about: Marble shooters run one law: a chain rolls, you shoot, three of a color bursts. This collection carries every windows build of that law in the catalogue - zuma deluxe and zuma's revenge, the full luxor line from the 2004 original to 5th passage, 10tons' sparkle and sparkle unleashed, and the portal-era variants beetle bug 3, karu and charma.
Zuma's two entries also sit in the popcap collection - a game can belong to more than one shelf, and the pages say so in their collections line.

collections.title: Racing
collections.caption: the full grid - street, circuit, combat, boat, kart and the classics the stores gave up on.
about: The racing shelf of the catalogue in one row: criterion's burnout and most wanted, black rock's split/second, bizarre's blur, the delisted driver san francisco, the nfs black-box trilogy, sega's crazy taxi and sonic riders, midway's hydro thunder, the toy-scale laws of re-volt and rollcage stage ii, the vector unit pair, and the licensed oddities from hot wheels to crazy frog.
Flatout 2 was dug earlier and sits here too. A game can carry more than one collection membership - the pages list them all.

collections.title: PlayStation Portable
collections.caption: the psp vault - eight digs for ppsspp, from kratos' handheld diptych to the iron fist roster.
about: Every psp dig the catalogue carries, played on windows through ppsspp: kingdom hearts birth by sleep, dante's inferno, the 3rd birthday, bleach heat the soul 7, the naruto shippuden pair, soulcalibur broken destiny, tekken 6 and ready at dawn's two god of war chapters.
Each page states its rom source and links the emulator; the one-platform law keeps the psp build as the dug version - no phantom windows ports, no ps3/xbox lists.

collections.title: PlayStation 2
collections.caption: the ps2 vault - twenty digs for pcsx2, from the colossus to the banned sequel.
about: Every ps2 dig the catalogue carries, played on windows through pcsx2: the god of war pair, shadow of the colossus, kingdom hearts ii, yakuza 2, shinobido, crash twinsanity, the licensed shelf from kim possible to the grim adventures, capcom's cel-shaded auto modellista, downhill domination, bmx xxx and the windows-cancelled manhunt 2.
The one-platform law applies down the line - each page digs exactly one console build.

collections.title: PlayStation
collections.caption: the ps1 vault - four digs for duckstation, theme parks to gunboats.
about: Every ps1 dig the catalogue carries, played on windows through duckstation: tom and jerry in house trap, jackie chan adventures, walt disney world quest magical racing tour and psygnosis' shipwreckers.
Small vault, honest scope - the catalogue grows one dig at a time.

collections.title: Wii
collections.caption: the wii vault - five digs for dolphin, from galaxy 2 to the zanpakuto duels.
about: Every wii dig the catalogue carries, played on windows through dolphin: donkey kong country returns, super mario galaxy 2, new super mario bros wii, the twilight princess & skyward sword pair and bleach shattered blade.
No wii u, no switch - the vault documents the wii itself.

multi_collections.title: Console Vaults
multi_collections.caption: the four console shelves of the catalogue - one collection per machine, one emulator law for all.
about: The console digs live in per-machine collections - playstation, playstation 2, playstation portable and wii - each page played on windows through its official emulator: duckstation, pcsx2, ppsspp and dolphin. The multi-collection below is the door to all four.

The one-platform law: each game digs as one platform - native windows when a windows build exists, the one supported console when it does not. ps3, ps4, xbox, wii u, switch and anything phone-shaped stay outside the vaults.
